lee: quick follow-up to the quant profiles RFC - saw a crash in canary when loader did a post-load per-layer requant and the runtime had already bound kernels.
anika: ouch. crash logs?
lee: assertion from kernel_selector: dtype mismatch at op conv1. loader rewrote weights to 4-bit after bind.
cole: sounds like we need a tiny loader<->runtime contract: loader must announce intended bitwidth surface before bind.
anika: can we do a cheap announce instead of full rebind? rebind is heavy on warmup.
cole: propose two-paths: ANNOUNCE (declare allowed bitwidths, runtime reserves kernels) and REBIND (force kernel reselection). ANNOUNCE is default.
lee: sample manifest header I sketched: {quant_announce: true, allowed: ["fp8","int8","4bit"], mode: "announce", max_rebind_ms: 200, hysteresis_ms: 250}
anika: good. what happens if runtime refuses announce (capacity/slo)?
cole: runtime returns a status code: ACCEPT / REFUSE_REBIND / FALLBACK_SUGGEST. structured error e.g. QUANT_ANNOUNCE_REFUSED with suggested_profiles.
lee: ops needs telemetry: emit quant_announced, announce_latency_ms, kernels_reserved, announce_fail_rate. tag with model_id, device_type.
anika: add cooldown per model to avoid thrash (hysteresis_ms).
deploy-bot: note: "deployed handshake proto to canary cluster - watch canary/quant-handshake" :rocket: 
cole: next: I'll open PR for handshake proto + runtime.can_support(manifest) API. anika: i'll add SRE alerts and test harness. lee: i'll update RFC appendix. target canary by Tue.
lee: thanks all, closing thread.
